subject: Biotechnology
title: Non-Invasive Prenatal Testing
description: A 60-second lesson on Non-Invasive Prenatal Testing.

hook.text: Fetal DNA floats in a pregnant mother's blood — a simple blood draw can detect Down syndrome without amniocentesis.

buildup.text: Cell-free fetal DNA makes up 10 to 20% of maternal plasma by the tenth week — sequencing counts chromosome fragments.

discovery.text: Excess chromosome 21 fragments indicate trisomy 21 — NIPT detects Down syndrome with over 99% sensitivity.

twist.text: False positives occur — confined placental mosaicism or maternal copy number variants mimic fetal abnormalities.

climax.text: NIPT now screens for microdeletions and single-gene disorders — expanding beyond trisomies to hundreds of conditions.

punchline.text: A blood test replaces a needle — NIPT makes prenatal screening safe and simple.

quiz.question: What causes false positives in NIPT?
options: The mother's DNA interferes with all fetal DNA detection
Confined placental mosaicism or maternal copy number variants can mimic fetal abnormalities
The test cannot distinguish between chromosomes 21 and 18
